stemMd: Starch and cellulose are both glucose polymers. Why can their biological properties nevertheless differ greatly?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Their glucose residues are joined with different glycosidic configurations.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The glucose molecules in cellulose contain no oxygen.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Starch consists entirely of amino acids.

explanationMd: The type and orientation of glycosidic linkage influence chain shape, intermolecular interactions and enzyme recognition. Sharing a monomer does not make two polymers structurally or functionally identical.

distractorRationale.b: Glucose retains oxygen in either polymer.
